Adele Bernice (Jeppesen) Morrison

October 21, 1917 – September 7, 1977

The Council Bluffs girl who soloed an airplane in 1938, married her flight instructor, and followed TWA across the country.

Born
October 21, 1917, Council Bluffs, Iowa; baptized December 9, 1917
Parents
Knud Wilhelm “Bill” Jeppesen (born in Denmark) and Anna Leonora (Hansen) Jeppesen
Childhood home
2705 South 7th Street, Council Bluffs, Iowa
Married
John R. Morrison Jr., June 7, 1939, Council Bluffs, Iowa
Died
September 7, 1977, Los Gatos Community Hospital, Los Gatos, California
Buried
Cedar Lawn Cemetery, Council Bluffs, Iowa (September 10, 1977)

A Council Bluffs childhood

Adele Bernice Jeppesen was born on October 21, 1917, in Council Bluffs, Iowa, and was baptized that December 9. Her father, Knud Wilhelm Jeppesen — “Bill” — had emigrated from Denmark; her mother, Anna Leonora (Hansen) Jeppesen, was Iowa-born of Danish stock. The family home was 2705 South 7th Street in Council Bluffs, the house where Adele grew up alongside her brothers, Donald Wilhelm and Franklin Bernard.

School days

Adele’s hand was trained early: she earned a Palmer penmanship certificate on May 28, 1931, at thirteen. She attended Abraham Lincoln High School in Council Bluffs and received her diploma on June 7, 1935 — the diploma itself spells her surname “Jeppeson,” one of several spellings the family name collected in American records. In 1935 she was also chosen May Queen at Abraham Lincoln, the title the newspapers would reach for three years later when she learned to fly.

Learning to fly

After school Adele went to work in the Premium Department of an insurance company. In the spring of 1938 she took her first airplane ride — and liked it so well that she decided to learn to fly herself. After just eight hours of dual instruction she soloed at the Council Bluffs airport in July 1938, and the Council Bluffs Nonpareil reported it on July 31, 1938 under the headline “May Queen Turns Flier”: she was the first Council Bluffs girl to complete a solo flight at the local airport.

She joined the Ninety-Nines, the women pilots’ organization, as a junior (student-pilot) member in February 1939, having first appeared as a visitor the previous October. She went on to earn her pilot’s license, as her son John William recounts.

Marriage

Her flight instructor was John R. Morrison Jr. On June 7, 1939 — two years to the day after her high-school graduation — Adele married him at Our Savior’s Lutheran Church in Council Bluffs, as the family’s marriage certificate and the newspaper wedding article both record. The Rev. E. W. Pedrussen officiated; Vivian Hansen was her bridesmaid and Richard Olsen the best man. After a honeymoon trip to Kansas City, the couple’s first home was at Drake Court in Omaha. One conflict is kept as a conflict: the Iowa marriage return places the marriage at Neola, not Council Bluffs — the certificate and the wedding article say Council Bluffs, and the discrepancy is noted rather than smoothed over.

The moving years

Marriage to an airline pilot meant a life of moves. In 1941 the family was in Kansas City, Missouri, at 535 Gladstone Boulevard — the address Adele gave that July when she filed her delayed birth certificate. During John’s wartime Navy service the family’s permanent address was 311 East 27th Avenue, North Kansas City. After the war came Mission, Kansas — the house at 5312 Rosewood Drive, where the family was photographed on the porch in October 1953. In fall 1954 TWA took them east to Westfield, New Jersey (414 Longfellow Avenue), and around 1961 west again to Saratoga, California, at 20169 Chateau Drive — the home where Adele spent her last sixteen years.

Her death

Adele died on September 7, 1977, at Los Gatos Community Hospital in Los Gatos, California, of a respiratory arrest due to a brain stem infarct; she was 59. Her funeral was held at Our Savior Lutheran Church in San Jose, and she was buried on September 10, 1977, at Cedar Lawn Cemetery in Council Bluffs, in the city where she was born. Cedar Lawn is her burial place — not, as some summaries have implied, her place of death.

Every image below is a real photograph or document from the family archive — no illustrations. Sensitive documents (certificates of death, licenses, passports) are described in the text but not reproduced here.

Sources and open questions

  • Birth: Iowa delayed certificate of birth no. 48766, filed July 1941 on Adele’s own affidavit, supported by a nurse’s statement, a doctor’s office record, her high school record, and a baptismal record — birth October 21, 1917, Council Bluffs; baptism December 9, 1917; father Knud W. Jeppesen, mother Anna L. Hansen.
  • Marriage place: the family certificate and the wedding article place the June 7, 1939 marriage at Our Savior’s Lutheran Church, Council Bluffs; the Iowa marriage return says Neola. Both readings are kept.
  • Pilot’s license: she earned her pilot’s license, on the account of her son John William; the license document itself is not among the archive papers. Her July 1938 solo flight is documented in the Nonpareil, and her Ninety-Nines junior membership in the organization’s newsletters.
  • A birth-date discrepancy: her 1958 New Jersey driver’s license shows a partly covered birth date reading “10.17” against the documented October 21. Unresolved.
  • An informant’s slip: her California death certificate names her mother as “Ann Schultz” — Schultz was the maiden name of her grandmother Kirsten (Schultz) Hansen. Her mother was Anna (Hansen) Jeppesen, as her birth and baptismal records show.
  • Spelling: records spell the family name Jeppesen, Jeppeson and Jeppessen; the forms are quoted as written in each source.
